content: Avoid deeply nested loops over large datasets This causes O(n^2) or worse performance will fail under high traffic
Avoid blocking I/O or synchronous operations inside request/response paths. This reduces concurrency and scalability.
Database queries must be indexed properly. Full table scans do not scale beyond moderate data sizes.
Avoid uncontrolled global variables or growing in-memory structures. This may cause memory leaks under long uptime.
All user input must be validated and sanitized before processing or database writes.
Proper error handling is required. Uncaught exceptions can crash the system at scale.
Shared mutable state in concurrent systems may cause race conditions and unpredictable behavior.
Highly coupled modules are hard to maintain and refactor after system growth.
